topic: Scarcity, constraints, rationality; normative/descriptive/prescriptive questions
assessment: Chapter1 explains all three questions and separates rationality from selfishness; Chapter2 specifies the feasible choice and opportunity cost.

topic: Context effects: arrow, decoy, framing, donation defaults, valuation, Mars bars, watched eyes
assessment: Examples have distinct mechanisms and evidence grades; commercial anecdotes and watched-eyes evidence are not presented as universal causal laws.

topic: Decision process; prediction versus valuation; opportunity cost; decision versus outcome quality
assessment: The map is explained through a choice and its information; ex ante quality is separated from realized outcome. Practice elicits alternatives, beliefs, values and a review rule.

topic: Subjective value, self/social relevance, implicit egotism, emotion, body, price-placebo, motives
assessment: Chapter6 develops neural valuation, automatic appraisal, self relevance, emotion and bodily-state mechanisms. Price and discount studies are concrete; evolutionary and current mechanisms are kept separate.

topic: Choice blindness, introspection limits, rationalization, premortems and feedback
assessment: Choice-blindness evidence distinguishes reports from causes; Chapter41 gives independent forecasts, records and structured review rather than a promise that introspection reveals causes.

topic: Predictive perception, priors, contextual inference, visual illusions, sensory limits
assessment: Chapter4 supplies explanatory illusions and a bounded predictive-processing account. Sensory differences belong in3. Neural network development is supplementary, not proof that all cognition follows one settled model.

topic: Placebo/nocebo, ability beliefs, aging expectations, stereotype threat, Pygmalion loops
assessment: Chapter5 covers bodily and interpersonal expectation pathways with replication/selection boundaries. Historic observational health associations do not establish that a belief alone causes longevity.

topic: Internal models as useful predictions and potential traps; disagreement
assessment: Book distinguishes useful priors from evidence-resistant beliefs; communication checks interpretations rather than asserting observers directly see one objective meaning.

topic: Limited attention, top-down/bottom-up selection, inattentional/change blindness, HUD and advertising
assessment: Chapter3 develops selective attention with studies and applications, including task-switching and notifications; figures expose missed information. Many demonstration screenshots are illustrations, not separate theories.

topic: System1/System2, controlled effort, automaticity and skilled intuition
assessment: Chapter8 retains conventional terms with process rather than brain-box interpretation, Stroop and CRT; expertise conditions and habit distinction are explicit.

topic: Heuristics, substitution, affect, availability and ease of retrieval
assessment: Chapter9 develops the panda/sea-star contrast, availability and retrieval ease with separate mechanisms; Chapter8 covers adaptive fit.

topic: Confirmation, Barnum/Forer effect
assessment: Chapter10 describes selective testing, generic personal descriptions and rival contributors to apparent accuracy; this differs from expectations changing outcomes in5.

topic: Three forms of overconfidence, planning fallacy and outside view
assessment: All three forms are defined at the same conceptual level; planning fallacy is an application. The lecture megaproject 0.5% headline need not replace the published planning-fallacy evidence already used.

topic: Anchoring, coherent arbitrariness, halo/horns and order effects
assessment: Chapter11 has random-anchor procedure and estimates plus context comparisons. Personal/classroom elicitation examples are not treated as fresh published experiments.

topic: Framing, presupposition and misinformation
assessment: Equivalent descriptions, question assumptions and memory distortion are distinguished; Asian-disease choice proportions and Loftus-Palmer results substantiate claims.

topic: Priming, affective context, exposure and familiarity
assessment: Semantic priming and repeated familiarity are developed; broad social/behavioral priming is not generalized from demonstrations. Unpublished in-class happy/sad results are not population estimates.

topic: CRT, Stroop, reflection and process redesign
assessment: Tasks have interpretive limits; redesign exercise matches a failure to a safeguard rather than claiming deliberation always corrects it.

topic: Goal-directed/habitual control, CIAO, popcorn, automaticity trajectory
assessment: Chapter21 develops cue-response learning, outcome sensitivity and context; Lally range is time to95% of modeled plateau, not a fixed habit deadline.

topic: Wanting/liking, dopamine learning, surprise, habituation, uncertainty, effort
assessment: Current text distinguishes neuronal firing from release/pleasure, prediction errors from habituation, cue prediction from habitual control, and uncertainty signals from attraction to all uncertainty.

topic: Stroop, access-dependent craving, cigarette/water, BRAIN and lapse response
assessment: Book contains flight and laboratory studies, their different designs, and a practical noticing sequence. Perceived opportunity is not equated with visual presence of cigarettes.

topic: Willpower, B=MAP, Tiny Habits, friction, ability, prompts, celebration, changed context
assessment: B=MAP is identified as a diagnostic framework; celebration guidance is distinguished from direct dopamine evidence; fresh-start and relocation findings carry design limitations.

topic: Choice architecture/nudge distinction; cafeteria placement
assessment: General distinction and welfare/avoidance conditions are covered. The Thorndike cafeteria evidence in slide36 was absent and is now incorporated with purchase-share denominators and study-design limits.
action: Added one study paragraph in the existing action-feasibility section: sequential label/placement phases, beverage-purchase share contrast3.4vs0.3percentage points, nonrandomized/sales boundary. No new diagram.

topic: WOOP, mental contrasting, implementation intentions, vaccination planning
assessment: WOOP components are operationalized and connected to goal-attainment meta-analysis; Milkman vaccination field experiment already provides the planning result.

topic: Whose goals, COM-B, temptation bundling, defensive interaction, evaluation
assessment: COM-B stays in a lens; desire/ability/opportunity diagnosis and support are not equated to one validated package. Intervention and actual outcome are distinguished.

topic: Strategic interdependence and Keynesian beauty contest
assessment: Chapter23 fully explains anticipation of others and market guesses; Chapter27 develops price feedback with empirical studies and alternative explanations.

topic: Meeting task and focal points
assessment: Relatable concert opening and focal-point reasoning replace arbitrary city-specific rewards. Chapter24 distinguishes focality, shared knowledge and payoff dominance.

topic: Guessing game, level-k, cognitive hierarchy and neural evidence
assessment: Chapter23 works through iterative reasoning and distinguishes level-k from population-mixture beliefs. Neural correlates are not used to label fixed intellectual types.

topic: Players, strategies, payoffs, best responses, dominance and equilibrium; identity game exercise
assessment: Basic concepts introduced in23, matrices developed in24/25 as requested; equilibrium is a conditional model claim, not a finding that people always optimize.

topic: Prisoner dilemma, third-party rules, repeated games, TFT, reputation, Golden Balls
assessment: Chapter25 has explicit incentive logic, noisy reciprocity, public goods/social preferences and stake/time boundaries; game-show evidence is not interchangeable with controlled random assignment.

topic: Coordination, conventions/QWERTY, stag hunt, risk/payoff dominance, chicken, volunteer dilemma, battle of sexes and commitment
assessment: All main coordination problems are developed, including mixed interests and credible commitment; illustrative standards history does not prove efficiency or inevitability.

topic: Price war/price guarantees, auctions and escalation
assessment: Strategic commitments and dollar-auction escalation are covered; conditional market effects matter. No need to repeat payoff analysis in the new social-influence chapter.

topic: Repeated appendix material and history/game demonstrations
assessment: Large trailing sections repeat earlier concepts; not independent missing curriculum. Final low-text payoff matrices still require visual inspection for exact cells.
action: Consolidate concepts, preserve exercise examples only when they contribute an additional distinction.

topic: Market efficiency, FOMC/news, September11, Challenger and event-study logic
assessment: Chapter27 already develops surprise versus announcement, unfolding information, relative-price inference and joint-test issues with named studies.

topic: Postearnings drift, size/value, momentum/reversal, benchmarks and costs
assessment: The chapter presents numerical historical comparisons, difference between raw and abnormal returns, risk-model alternatives and implementability.

topic: Technical/fundamental analysis, CAPM/factors, arithmetic/geometric returns, CUBA, triangular arbitrage, Palm/3Com
assessment: These examples and formal relations are substantially developed in27; mental accounting/myopic loss aversion belongs in19. Historical return pictures are not forecasting guarantees.

topic: In-class fish/asset experiment and archived payment rules
assessment: Experimental-market interpretation belongs in27/methods. Session interface instructions, payment rules and unreported student data are not publication evidence.
action: Exclude logistics and unverified class estimates; retain the public experimental concepts.

topic: Assets, payouts, constant-growth valuation and finite-horizon benchmark
assessment: The chapter works expected dividends and discounted values, separating risk-neutral expected payoff from guaranteed value.

topic: Resale feedback, historical bubbles, housing, excess volatility and flash crashes
assessment: Historical claims are qualified; bubbles/crashes/systemic crises are differentiated. Crash alone is not proof of prior irrational price.

topic: Laboratory markets,304traders, overlapping generations, flat fundamentals, liquidity and credit
assessment: Current chapter distinguishes design variants and supports liquidity/experience claims with studies. Unpublished classroom plot on28 remains an illustration only.

topic: Expectations, gender composition, strategy heterogeneity, lottery assets and limits to arbitrage
assessment: Current chapter reports heterogeneous/conditional gender results and model-dependent trader classifications instead of inferring types directly from aggregate prices.

assessment: Appendix uses positive-expectations example, explicitly motivating a tension and a researchable question; ABT is a writing tool, not a proven persuasion law.
